sentences.text: Shri Kamal Kumar Rochalani- Advocate appearing on  Vandana Kekre- Advocate for respondent No.3/Insurance Compan  ORDER 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants-claimants challenging the award dated 02.04.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia (M.P.), in Claim Case No. 124/2018, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.
2. The date of the accident, the finding of negligence, and the liability are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality, as the same have not been challenged in the present appeal.

3. As per the impugned award, the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,99,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization on account of the death of Megh Singh in the motor accident.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants, while assailing the impugned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10630 2 MA-3632-2019 award, submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased, which is on the lower side.

It is contended that the prior to alleged accident, deceased was engaged in agricultural activities, used to operate a harvester, reaper and tractor as well as engaged in farming by which, deceased used to Smt Urmila Rawat vs Pradeep Kumar on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16874723/
1 earn Rs.30,000 - Rs.40,000/- per month; however, the said aspect has not been properly appreciated by the learned Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: Smt Urmila Rawat vs Pradeep Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the assessment of income by treating the deceased on lower side is erroneous and, on this ground, enhancement of compensation has been sought.
It is contended on behalf of appellants that Claims Tribunal has also committed error in not awarding reasonable amount in other heads i.e. loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

With regard to the assessment of income, the learned Claims Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month on the ground that no documentary evidence regarding his income was produced.

However, the record reflects that the deceased was engaged in agricultural activities, used to operate a harvester, reaper and tractor as well as engaged in farming and the claimants have produced material in support thereof.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased ought to be assessed in accordance with the Minimum Wages applicable to a semi-skilled worker.

Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as an semi- skilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.8,182/- per NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10630 3 MA-3632-2019 month.

8. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 25% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 13 has rightly been applied by Claims Tribunal.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Claimants are also entitled to get consortium in the light of the judgment passed by Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur and others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131 .

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur and others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal up to this extent be set aside and the reasonable amount of compensation be awarded by adding reasonable amount of compensation under, loss of consortium, loss of estate and other heads etc.
10.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
HEAD   Income Rs.8182 x   Future Prospects@ 25% Rs.1,22,73

After deducting Dependency 1/3 Rs.81,820/
 Multiplier 13 Rs.10,63,6  Other Heads:-
 Medical Bill Rs.1,09,00 Smt Urmila Rawat vs Pradeep Kumar on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16874723/
2  Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000   Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/

Total Compensation = Rs.13,22,660/-
11.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10630 4 MA-3632-2019 comes to Rs.13,22,660/- as against the sum of Rs.6,99,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.6,23,660/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
12. In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award i s modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.6,23,660/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

13. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
14. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
